activities.anchor: Functional MRI does not measure neurons
activities.caption: rebuild the BOLD chain — from firing to voxel test
activities.name: bimBoldOrder

config.prompt: Between a thought and a blob sits a chain of proxies. Rebuild it:
items: Local blood flow rises to overcompensate
The changing ratio of oxygenated to deoxygenated haemoglobin alters local magnetisation
A general linear model convolves the predicted neural timecourse with the haemodynamic response function
Each voxel is tested for condition-related variance
config.why: The haemodynamic response peaks roughly 4–6 seconds after firing and decays over ~12 — the blood, not the machine, is the temporal bottleneck at every link of the chain.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — how to read a blob
activities.name: bimBlobSpot

config.prompt: A student's summary of what an fMRI blob is contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: A statistical map is a test statistic thresholded across roughly 100,000 voxels.
Multiple-comparison correction keeps the false-positive rate under control.
The surviving blob is a spotlight on the faculty for trust — read the mental state straight off it.
'Activation' means increased metabolic demand — a net of excitation, inhibition and local field potentials.
config.correction: A blob is a thresholded statistic, not a spotlight on a faculty: activation supports many mental states — novelty, arousal, faces, reward — so reading one specific state from it is reverse inference.
config.why: Legitimate reverse inference exists only with quantified selectivity — activation-pattern overlap rates across a large task library — which is rarely what pop-neuroscience headlines have done.

activities.name: bimErpMatch

config.prompt: Time-locked averaging exposes components with names and jobs. Pair them:

pairs.right: band-limited power indexing arousal and attention

config.why: Event-related potentials give the millisecond timeline its vocabulary — each component a functional identity read straight out of the averaged epochs.

activities.anchor: the ceiling is informational, not instrumental
activities.caption: you need the seizure onset zone — what now?
activities.name: bimEegBranch

config.root: Clinical decision: a patient's seizure onset zone must be localised. Your EEG rig and its inverse problem stand between you and the answer.

choices.label: Double the electrode count — more sensors, more information
choices.feedback: More sensors feel like more information, and modern nets run past two hundred channels.

choices.label: Use EEG for what it owns — timing — and refer the spatial question to methods that measure space
choices.feedback: The productive division of labour: EEG tells you when, fMRI tells you roughly where.

sensors.text: Extra electrodes sample the two-dimensional shadow more finely without restoring the lost dimension — infinitely many 3-D current configurations still produce the same surface pattern, and even MEG inherits the ambiguity.

divide.text: Localisation is left to methods that measure space; combined EEG-fMRI studies exploit exactly this complement — milliseconds from one box, millimetres from the other.

config.why: The scalp records a two-dimensional shadow of three-dimensional current flow — the inverse problem caps localisation no matter how many electrodes you buy.

activities.anchor: Correlation cannot establish that a region is
activities.caption: file each method — watch only, or perturb
activities.name: bimCausalBuckets

config.prompt: Which methods only watch activity, and which can test necessity? File them:

items.label: fMRI BOLD recorded during a task
PET tracer binding mapped across the brain
a lesion — damage as a natural experiment
TMS: a magnetic pulse transiently disrupts a targeted patch
optogenetics: light-activated opsins excite or silence defined cell classes

config.why: Only the perturb family can argue necessity — the watching family measures what happens, never what the region is for.

activities.anchor: H.M.'s intact digit span showed working memory ran elsewhere
activities.caption: true or false — reading a spared function
activities.name: bimSparedJudge

statements.s: If a function survives a lesion, the damaged region was never involved in it.
statements.why: Lesions are uncontrolled in size and location, and the brain reorganises — compensation can mask a region's normal contribution.

statements.s: H.M.'s intact digit span showed the medial temporal lobe idle in healthy brains.
statements.why: It showed working memory ran elsewhere — absence of deficit is evidence, but far weaker than a clean double dissociation.

statements.s: Loss-of-function logic seems symmetric, but the caveats break the symmetry.
statements.why: Damage abolishing a function argues involvement; survival of a function does not prove irrelevance.

statements.s: TMS imports the lesion logic into healthy volunteers.
statements.why: A brief magnetic pulse makes a virtual lesion — causal, reversible, within-subject, with standing caveats of coarse focality and depth.

activities.anchor: the Ig-Nobel-winning point was that uncorrected voxelwise statistics
activities.caption: rebuild the audit — how the crisis became practice
activities.name: bimAuditOrder

config.prompt: The statistical reckoning arrived in a sequence. Rebuild it:
items: The dead salmon: a standard pipeline run on a scanned fish 'finds' activation once multiple-comparison correction is skipped
Vul and colleagues: overlapping analytic selections inflate brain-behaviour correlations
Eklund and colleagues: a widely used clusterwise correction violates a parametric assumption real data break
Corrective practice goes mainstream: family-wise error or false-discovery-rate control, preregistration, independent validation, data sharing
Scale arrives: UK Biobank and the Human Connectome Project run thousands of subjects, pulling estimates toward their true (usually smaller) sizes
config.why: Uncorrected voxelwise statistics manufacture signal from noise — the field's crisis was predictable from huge data and small samples, and the fix was institutional, not heroic.
